title: Stronger Agents Can Learn Weaker Skills
central_question: Can increasing execution-time test-time compute improve online task success while degrading the persistent skill learned from those executions because reusable failures are rescued before the updater observes them?
thesis: Acting-optimal compute need not be learning-optimal compute when the execution policy also generates the experience consumed by persistent self-evolution.

substrate.name: MindMemOS + SpreadsheetBench
substrate.why_low_is_three: The first-party skill prompt requests a skill-tool load before spreadsheet actions; three turns permit skill retrieval, one substantive tool action, and a final assistant turn without forcing premature truncation.
substrate.secondary_substrate: SkillEvolBench commit 9e3daa339987c3cfa624121e1be442593a53d43c; deferred because first-party Harbor job fixes n_attempts=1 and lacks an equally clean executor-compute knob

load_bearing_hypotheses.H4_missing_information: G_frozen(H_L_SHADOW) > G_frozen(H_H_HARDMINE) is required for the strong missing-counterfactual-information interpretation

scientific_unit: complete evolution run and its final learned skill state
episode_role: within-run experience only; episodes/repeats are not independent scientific units
